Anatomy-01.question: ১) Which one is the major constituent of plasma membrane?
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is protein. Proteins are the major constituent of the plasma membrane by mass and are responsible for most membrane functions.

Components of plasma membrane:

Protein (~50% by mass) → Transport, receptors, enzymes, cell signalling

Phospholipid (~40%) → Forms the lipid bilayer framework

Cholesterol → Maintains membrane fluidity and stability

Carbohydrate → Cell recognition and glycocalyx formation

The other options are incorrect because:

Phospholipid → Major structural component but not the major constituent by mass.

Cholesterol → Regulates fluidity, but present in smaller amounts.

Carbohydrate → Minor component attached to proteins/lipids.

High-yield cell biology recall:
Major constituent of plasma membrane (by mass) = Protein
Basic structural framework = Phospholipid bilayer

Exam pearl:
Plasma membrane = Lipid bilayer + proteins; proteins are the major functional component.

৩) Primary ossification centre are in
Anatomy-01.exp:
The primary ossification centre appears in the diaphysis (shaft) of a long bone during fetal life. Ossification begins in the centre of the shaft and later extends toward both ends.

  • Secondary ossification centres develop in the epiphysis after birth.

  • The epiphyseal plate (growth plate) is responsible for lengthwise growth of bone.

  • Metaphysis is the region between diaphysis and epiphysis where active bone growth occurs.

Exam pearl:

  • Primary ossification centre → Diaphysis (before birth)

  • Secondary ossification centre → Epiphysis (after birth)

  • Epiphyseal plate → Bone length growth

৯) Criteria of smooth muscle fiber excludes
Anatomy-01.exp:
Smooth muscle fibers are fusiform (spindle-shaped), non-striated, and unbranched. They are composed of a single elongated cell with a central nucleus. Smooth muscle cells are connected mainly by gap junctions, which allow electrical communication and coordinated contraction.

Why others are correct:

  • Fusiform  → Typical shape of smooth muscle cells.

  • No striation  → Smooth muscle lacks visible striations because actin and myosin are not arranged into sarcomeres.

  • No branching  → Smooth muscle fibers are generally unbranched.

Exam pearl:

  • Smooth muscle → Fusiform + Non-striated + Unbranched + Gap junctions

  • Cardiac muscle → Striated + Branched + Intercalated discs

  • Skeletal muscle → Striated + Long cylindrical fibers + Multinucleated

Anatomy-01.question: ১০) Packaging centre of the cell
১১) Organelle that contains hydrolytic digestive enzymes
১২) Osteocytes are found in
Anatomy-01.exp:
Osteocytes (mature bone cells) are found inside small spaces called lacunae within the bone matrix. Each osteocyte extends processes through canaliculi, which allow communication and exchange of nutrients with other bone cells.

Why others are incorrect:

  • Lamellae  → Layers of bone matrix arranged around central canals.

  • Canaliculi  → Tiny channels containing osteocyte processes, not the osteocytes themselves.

  • Matrix  → The hard extracellular substance of bone containing lacunae.

Exam pearl:

  • Osteocyte → Lacuna

  • Osteoblast → Bone-forming cell on bone surface

  • Osteoclast → Bone-resorbing cell

  • Canaliculi → Communication between osteocytes

Anatomy-01.question: ১৩) Which cytoskeletal component participates in muscle contraction?
১৪) Most abundant constituent of bone matrix
Anatomy-01.exp:
The most abundant inorganic constituent of bone matrix is calcium hydroxyapatite Ca10(PO4)6(OH)2Ca10​(PO4​)6​(OH)2​. It provides the hardness and strength of bone.

Bone matrix consists of:

  • Organic component → Mainly type I collagen (provides flexibility and tensile strength)

  • Inorganic component → Mainly calcium hydroxyapatite (provides rigidity and hardness)

Why others are incorrect:

  • Bicarbonate  → Present in small amounts as a mineral component.

  • Citrate  → Minor component of bone mineral.

  • Magnesium → Present in small quantity.

Exam pearl:

  • Most abundant inorganic salt of bone → Calcium hydroxyapatite

  • Most abundant organic component → Type I collagen

  • Osteoid → Unmineralized organic bone matrix

Anatomy-01.question: ১৫) Which cytoskeletal component stabilize junction between cells?
১৬) Intramembranous ossification mainly occurs in
Anatomy-01.exp:
Intramembranous ossification occurs mainly in flat bones, where bone develops directly from mesenchymal connective tissue without a cartilage model. It is responsible for the formation of many bones of the skull, facial bones, and clavicle.

Why others are incorrect:

  • Long bone → Mainly develops by endochondral ossification.

  • Short bone  → Mainly develops by endochondral ossification.

  • Sesamoid bone  → Develops by endochondral ossification within tendons.

Exam pearl:

  • Intramembranous ossification → Flat bones (skull, clavicle)

  • Endochondral ossification → Long bones, short bones, vertebrae, pelvis

  • Primary ossification centre → Diaphysis

  • Secondary ossification centre → Epiphysis

Anatomy-01.question: ১৭) Longest phase of cell cycle
১৮) DNA replication occurs in which phase of cell cycle?
১৯) How many daughter cells are formed during mitosis?
২০) Collagen type of Sharpey fiber
Anatomy-01.exp:
Sharpey’s fibers are bundles of Type I collagen fibers that extend from the periosteum into the bone matrix. They anchor the periosteum firmly to the underlying bone and provide strong attachment.

Why others are incorrect:

  • Type II collagen  → Found mainly in cartilage (especially hyaline cartilage).

  • Type III collagen  → Forms reticular fibers in organs and connective tissue.

  • Type IV collagen  → Found in basement membranes.

Exam pearl:

  • Sharpey fibers → Type I collagen

  • Cartilage → Type II collagen

  • Reticular fibers → Type III collagen

  • Basement membrane → Type IV collagen

Anatomy-01.question: ২২) Tissue with very small amount of extracellular matrix
Anatomy-01.exp:
Epithelial tissue contains a very small amount of extracellular matrix (ECM) because its cells are closely packed together with minimal intercellular space. Epithelial cells are mainly involved in covering, lining, secretion, and absorption.

Why others are incorrect:

  • Connective tissue  → Has abundant extracellular matrix containing fibers and ground substance.

  • Muscle tissue  → Has more ECM than epithelium, though less than connective tissue.

  • Nervous tissue  → Has supporting cells and some ECM; not the tissue with the least ECM.

Exam pearl:

  • Least extracellular matrix → Epithelium

  • Most extracellular matrix → Connective tissue

  • Epithelial tissue → Cells tightly packed + basement membrane

Anatomy-01.question: ২৩) Type of epithelium in developing ovarian follicle
Anatomy-01.exp:
The epithelium (follicular/granulosa cell layer) of a developing ovarian follicle is initially simple cuboidal epithelium. As the follicle matures, the granulosa cells proliferate and become multiple layers (stratified appearance), forming the mature follicle.

Why others are incorrect:

  • Stratified cuboidal  → Not the typical early epithelial lining of developing ovarian follicles.

  • Simple columnar  → Found in some absorptive/secretory surfaces, not ovarian follicles.

  • Stratified columnar  → Rare epithelium, not present in ovarian follicle development.

Exam pearl:

  • Developing ovarian follicle → Simple cuboidal epithelium

  • Mature ovarian follicle → Multiple layers of granulosa cells

  • Ovary surface epithelium → Simple cuboidal ("germinal epithelium")

২৯) Where duct is usually short or absent?
Anatomy-01.exp:
In branched acinar (alveolar) glands, the duct is usually short or may be absent because the secretory portions open directly into a short duct system. A typical example is the sebaceous gland, which often has a short duct opening into a hair follicle.

Why others are incorrect:

  • Simple tubular  → Has a distinct unbranched tubular secretory portion with a duct.

  • Branched tubular  → Has branched secretory tubules connected to a duct.

  • Coiled tubular  → Sweat glands have a coiled secretory part with a long duct opening onto the skin.

Exam pearl:

  • Short/absent duct → Sebaceous gland (branched acinar)

  • Long duct → Sweat gland (simple coiled tubular)

  • Compound glands → Branched duct system

৩১) Which cell produces antibody?
৩২) Most common cell in connective tissue proper
Anatomy-01.exp:
Fibroblasts are the most common cells in connective tissue proper. They are responsible for producing and maintaining the extracellular matrix, including:

  • Collagen fibers

  • Elastic fibers

  • Reticular fibers

  • Ground substance

Why others are incorrect:

  • Plasma cell → Produces antibodies (immunoglobulins), but is less abundant.

  • Macrophage→ Performs phagocytosis and antigen presentation.

  • Adipocyte → Stores fat and is present in adipose tissue, not the most common cell of connective tissue proper.

Exam pearl:

  • Most abundant cell in connective tissue proper → Fibroblast

  • Antibody production → Plasma cell

  • Phagocytosis → MacrophageHistamine release → Mast cell

Anatomy-01.question: ৩৩) Major location of Dendritic cell is
Anatomy-01.exp:
The major location of dendritic cells is the skin, where they are known as Langerhans cells. They act as antigen-presenting cells (APCs) and capture foreign antigens, then migrate to lymph nodes to activate T lymphocytes.

Why others are incorrect:

  • CNS  → Contains microglia, which are macrophage-like immune cells, not typical dendritic cells.

  • Bone  → Contains osteocytes, osteoblasts, and osteoclasts.

  • Lymph node  → Dendritic cells are present here as antigen-presenting cells, but their major classic location is skin (Langerhans cells).

Exam pearl:

  • Dendritic cell in skin → Langerhans cell

  • Main function → Antigen presentation to T cells

  • Most potent APC → Dendritic cell

  • Macrophage → Phagocytosis + antigen presentation

Anatomy-01.question: ৩৪) Which type of fiber is abundant in immune system?
Anatomy-01.exp:
This network supports immune cells and provides a scaffold for their movement and interaction.

Why others are incorrect:

  • Collagen → Mainly provides tensile strength in connective tissues; not the characteristic fiber of immune organs.

  • Elastic  → Provides elasticity in tissues like large arteries and lungs.

  • All of them  → Reticular fibers are the predominant supportive fibers in lymphoid organs.

Exam pearl:

  • Immune organs → Reticular fibers (Type III collagen)

  • Skin/tendon/ligament strength → Type I collagen

  • Cartilage → Type II collagen

  • Basement membrane → Type IV collagen

Anatomy-01.question: ৩৫) One Haversian canal is attached to other through
৩৬) Which one is immature bone?
৩৭) Patella is related to tendon of
Anatomy-01.exp:
The patella is a sesamoid bone embedded within the tendon of the quadriceps femoris muscle. It increases the mechanical advantage of the quadriceps during knee extension.

The quadriceps tendon attaches to the base and sides of the patella, and continues as the patellar ligament to attach to the tibial tuberosity.

Why others are incorrect:

  • Sartorius  → Inserts on the medial surface of the tibia (pes anserinus).

  • Adductor longus  → Inserts on the linea aspera of femur.

  • Tibialis anterior  → Inserts on medial cuneiform and base of 1st metatarsal.

Exam pearl:

  • Patella → Sesamoid bone in quadriceps tendon

  • Largest sesamoid bone → Patella

  • Main function → Improves leverage of quadriceps for knee extension

৪৩) Differentiated cells of which tissue cannot undergo mitosis?
Anatomy-01.exp:
Fully differentiated nerve cells (neurons) generally cannot undergo mitosis because they are terminally differentiated and remain in the G₀ phase of the cell cycle. Once mature neurons are formed, they lose the ability to divide.

Why others are incorrect:

  • Epithelium  → Has high regenerative capacity and actively undergoes mitosis.

  • Bones  → Osteoblasts and osteoprogenitor cells can divide and help in bone growth and repair.

  • Skeletal muscle  → Mature muscle fibers cannot divide, but satellite cells can proliferate and regenerate muscle.

Exam pearl:

  • Permanent cells (do not divide) → Neurons, cardiac muscle cells

  • Stable cells (can divide when needed) → Bone, smooth muscle, liver

  • Labile cells (continuously dividing) → Epithelium, bone marrow

Anatomy-01.question: ৪৪) What type of epiphysis is present in coracoids process of scapula?
৪৫) Uniaxial joint
Anatomy-01.exp:
A uniaxial joint allows movement around one axis only. The elbow joint is a hinge type synovial joint and permits mainly flexion and extension, making it a uniaxial joint.

Why others are incorrect:

  • Wrist  → Biaxial (condyloid/ellipsoid) joint; allows flexion, extension, abduction, and adduction.

  • Hip  → Multiaxial (ball and socket) joint.

  • Shoulder  → Multiaxial (ball and socket) joint.

Exam pearl:

  • Uniaxial → Hinge & pivot joints

    • Elbow (hinge)

    • Interphalangeal joints (hinge)

    • Atlanto-axial joint (pivot)

  • Biaxial → Wrist (condyloid), thumb CMC (saddle)

  • Multiaxial → Shoulder & hip (ball and socket)

Anatomy-01.question: ৪৬) Bone remodelling cell
Anatomy-01.exp:
Osteoclasts are the major cells involved in bone remodelling by causing bone resorption (breakdown of bone matrix). They are large multinucleated cells derived from the monocyte–macrophage lineage and contain tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase (TRAP).

Bone remodelling involves:

  1. Osteoclast → Bone resorption

  2. Osteoblast → New bone formation

  3. Osteocyte → Maintains bone matrix

Why others are incorrect:

  • Osteoprogenitor  → Stem cells that give rise to osteoblasts.

  • Osteoblast→ Responsible for bone formation, not resorption.

  • Osteocytes  → Mature bone cells that maintain bone tissue.

Exam pearl:

  • Bone resorption → Osteoclast

  • Bone formation → Osteoblast

  • Bone maintenance → Osteocyte

  • Bone remodelling → Osteoclast + Osteoblast (main pair)

Anatomy-01.question: ৪৭) Which type of epithelium has umbrella cell?
Anatomy-01.exp:
Umbrella cells (surface/umbrella cells) are characteristic of transitional epithelium (urothelium). These are large, dome-shaped cells present in the superficial layer and allow the epithelium to stretch and accommodate changes in volume.

Locations of transitional epithelium:

  • Urinary bladder

  • Ureter

  • Renal pelvis

Why others are incorrect:

  • Simple squamous  → Found in alveoli, endothelium, mesothelium.

  • Pseudostratified  → Found mainly in respiratory tract and epididymis.

  • Stratified cuboidal  → Found in ducts of sweat glands and larger glands.

Exam pearl:

  • Umbrella cells → Transitional epithelium

  • Function → Distension + protection in urinary tract

  • Example → Urinary bladder

Anatomy-01.question: ৪৮) Anchoring junctions are produced by
Anatomy-01.exp:
Anchoring junctions (adherens junctions and desmosomes) are mainly formed by cadherins, which are calcium-dependent cell adhesion molecules. They provide strong attachment between adjacent cells.

  • Adherens junction → Cadherin linked to actin filaments

  • Desmosome → Desmoglein/desmocollin (cadherins) linked to intermediate filaments

Why others are incorrect:

  • Occludin  → Component of tight junctions; helps seal intercellular space.

  • Claudin  → Major protein of tight junctions.

  • Actin  → Cytoskeletal protein that attaches to adherens junctions but does not form the junction itself.

Exam pearl:

  • Anchoring junction → Cadherin

  • Tight junction → Claudin + Occludin

  • Gap junction → Connexin

  • Hemidesmosome → Integrin

Anatomy-01.question: ৪৯) Stereocillia are found in
Anatomy-01.exp:
Stereocilia are long, non-motile microvilli-like structures found in the inner ear, especially in hair cells of the organ of Corti and vestibular apparatus, where they help in mechanosensation (hearing and balance).

Why others are incorrect:

  • Conjunctiva  → Contains stratified columnar/stratified squamous epithelium with goblet cells, not stereocilia.

  • Sweat gland  → Has simple coiled tubular epithelium; no stereocilia.

  • Cornea  → Has non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium.

Exam pearl:

  • Stereocilia → Epididymis + inner ear hair cells

  • Cilia → Respiratory tract, uterine tube

  • Microvilli → Intestine (brush border), kidney tubules

  • Stereocilia are modified long microvilli, not true cilia

Anatomy-01.question: ৫০) Cristae is a characteristic of
Anatomy-01.exp:
Cristae are characteristic folds of the inner mitochondrial membrane. They increase the surface area of the inner membrane, allowing more space for:

  • Electron transport chain

  • ATP synthase

  • Oxidative phosphorylation

Why others are incorrect:

  • Golgi apparatus  → Contains cisternae involved in protein and lipid modification.

  • Lysosome  → Contains hydrolytic digestive enzymes.

  • Ribosome  → Responsible for protein synthesis.

Exam pearl:

  • Cristae → Inner mitochondrial membrane

  • Matrix → Contains mitochondrial DNA, ribosomes, enzymes

  • Main function of mitochondria → ATP production (powerhouse of cell)
